references.text: The continuation of the story about Jerubbaal's house and how the Israelites treated his family after his death, which directly fulfills the prophecy in 8:35.
An explanation of why Gideon was called Jerubba'al—because he tore down Baal's altar.
A description of Gideon's victory over the Midianites—all the good he had done for Israel.
Gideon rejected kingship and pointed to the Lord as Israel's ruler—one of his good deeds for Israel.
Moses' rebuke of Israel for their ingratitude toward God—the same pattern of ingratitude shown toward Jerubbaal's house.
Samuel reminds the people of all the righteous acts the Lord performed for them and their ancestors—a parallel to Gideon's deeds.
